data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 requires adversarial items with surface-structure divergence as the distinguishing evidence but conflates two different reliability sources the problem asks about. On adversarial items, the single expert's causal understanding could also fail if the expert's mental model shares the same surface-correlation bias; conversely, the panel could succeed via aggregation cancelling errors even under mere compliance. SRC_001's 'if and only if' requires both that compliance fails and genuine reliability holds on adversarial items, but this conflates 'panel-genuine-reliability' with 'expert-genuine-reliability' — the comparison is panel-vs-expert, not genuine-vs-compliant. A panel relying on mere compliance could still outperform a single expert whose intuition is equally surface-correlated; SRC_001's adversarial test would reject the panel as 'mere compliance' even when it is genuinely more reliable than the expert. The framework mistakes evidence distinguishing compliance from understanding for evidence distinguishing panel reliability from expert reliability.
